questions.prompt: Monty Hall: three doors, one car. You pick one. Host opens a goat door. Switching wins with probability:
questions.explanation: Your first pick is right 1/3 of the time; the other unopened door then holds the car 2/3 of the time.

questions.prompt: About how many people do you need so that P(shared birthday) is about 50% (365 days, ignore leap years)?
questions.explanation: The birthday paradox: 23 people is about 50%.

questions.prompt: 1000 bottles, one poisoned. A test strip shows a result after a delay and can be reused only as a bit in one round. Minimum testers for one round of tests?
Why are manhole covers typically round?
options: A round cover cannot fall through its opening
They weigh less than any other shape
questions.explanation: The circle's width is constant; a square cover can be tilted through the diagonal.

questions.prompt: Two ropes each burn in 60 minutes, unevenly. You can light ends. How can you measure 45 minutes?
options: Light both ends of both ropes
Light both ends of rope A and one end of B; when A dies, light B's other end
questions.explanation: A finishes at 30 minutes. Lighting B's other end then burns the remaining 30-minute length in 15 minutes. Total 45.

questions.prompt: With jugs of 3 L and 5 L, can you measure exactly 4 L?
questions.explanation: Classic water-jug problem; 4 is a multiple of gcd(3,5)=1 and ≤ 5.

questions.prompt: Farmer, fox, chicken, grain: boat holds farmer plus one. First trip should take:
questions.explanation: Otherwise fox eats chicken or chicken eats grain.

questions.prompt: Hilbert's hotel is full. To free room 1 for one new guest, move occupant of room n to:
questions.explanation: Everyone shifts up one room; infinitely many rooms remain.

questions.prompt: 12 balls, one different weight (heavier or lighter). A balance scale. Minimum weighings in the worst case?
How many times do the hour and minute hands overlap in 12 hours?
questions.explanation: They overlap 11 times every 12 hours (they almost-meet around 11 and 12 as one event).

questions.prompt: 100 closed doors, 100 people. Person k toggles multiples of k. How many doors are open at the end?
questions.explanation: Door n is toggled d(n) times and ends open iff n is a square. There are 10 squares ≤ 100.

questions.prompt: 2 eggs, 100 floors, minimize worst-case drops. The optimal worst-case count is:
5 rational pirates, 100 indivisible coins. Most senior proposes a take-it-or-leave-it split; ties reject. How many coins does the most senior keep in the standard solution?
questions.explanation: A offers 98 to self, 0, 1, 0, 1 so two others still prefer A over the next game.

questions.prompt: A plane mirror appears to reverse left and right, not up and down, because it actually reverses:
questions.explanation: The mirror maps each point to the point opposite along the normal.

questions.prompt: 3 switches, 3 bulbs in another room. You may enter the bulb room once. A working strategy uses heat. After waiting, a bulb that is off but warm means:
options: Its switch was on earlier then turned off
questions.explanation: On for a while then off: warm and dark. Currently on: lit. Never on: cold and dark.
